rubric_notes: Evidence-backed families and members, homology endpoint cited, superfamily = probable common ancestry 'not identical function', H1/H5 correctly treated as no positive claim rather than evidence of absence, enzyme hits excluded, limits and background-knowledge disclosures clear. Weakness: asserts a.22.1.3 TAFs are 'the family closest to histones after the core family', an ordering SCOPe does not encode and which is unsupported. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Correct classifications and sunids with superfamily homology scope 'sf' verified. Superfamily-level remote homology stated with no family-level claim; rejects transfer of HisE activity, substrate and mechanism; treats superfamily active-site comment as not domain-specific; notes 7-93 boundary limits whole-protein inference; explicitly says different families are not evidence of nonhomology or convergence. Minor overstatement that SCOPe 'records no function for either' despite the HisE protein label, not material.

Correct families with sunids, shared parents (root > c > c.55 > c.55.1), superfamily homology record all supported. Clear inference of superfamily-level common ancestry with family-level homology not asserted; explicitly rejects shared role, substrate, reaction, ligand, mechanism, regulation, and template use; notes empty name searches are a search gap, not absence evidence (supported). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. All three families, sunids, superfamily a.25.1 (47240), fold a.25, class a verified against bundle; bimetal-centre comment, homology_implied_by_level flags, and Pfam PF05067 auto-mapping all supported. Interpretation: superfamily-level probable common ancestry with family-level functional divergence; refuses to transfer chemistry; explicitly rejects convergence/nonhomology reading; flags R1 (a.98.1, c.7.1) as unrelated name hits; states that mechanism or catalytic-residue claims need sequence/structure alignment or literature. Meets all must_include and must_avoid items.

Complete: all three families under b.6.1 with correct sunids, homology_scope 'sf', superfamily copper comment versus family-level 'lacking the metal-binding site' comments, d1iuza_ 'complexed with cu' annotation, b.18.1.4 receptor-domain distinction, d.126.1.5 catalytic domain. States remote common ancestry is not a functional statement and that copper/redox roles need experimental or literature evidence. Everything is supported by the bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

States the three sibling families under d.15.1 with sunids, Pfam xrefs and homology records all supported by the bundle; interprets as superfamily-level probable common ancestry, not shared family or function; rejects transfer of conjugation, UBX binding roles and Ras-effector binding, and warns against calling families analogs; notes family-level-only retrieval. Minor: refers to an internal tool name (get_scop_domains) but no factual error. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22. All three families, superfamily c.23.1 and fold c.23 verified via parents endpoints with sunids and KaiA domain SIDs; superfamily-level probable ancestry stated, fold adds nothing beyond it. Rejects receiver/phosphorelay transfer, ODC-wing catalysis, KaiA circadian/KaiC claims, and nonhomology/convergence claims. Correctly notes the linker and CASP5 comments are not functional annotations. Trivial imprecision: calls 82346 a protein node (it is the species node).

Correct b.84.5/b.84.5.1 placement under fold b.84 with sibling superfamilies b.84.1-b.84.4 and sunids. Clearly separates fold (architecture only) from superfamily (ancestry among b.84.5 members) and states that a separate superfamily withholds a homology claim without asserting analogy or convergence. Family grouping of Pyrococcus/Thermus/yeast bulge domains stated. Domain SIDs and boundaries match the bundle. Fold comment text is not in this answer's bundle but is the genuine b.84 annotation. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct f.21 split with all family sunids (56910, 81373, 103502/103503), fold core comment and fold homology warning bundle-supported. Correctly states homology is implied within each superfamily only, the split is no positive cross-superfamily assertion and not evidence of analogy/convergence, treats the f.21.3 possible-link and Pfam mapping as curator notes, and names the FATCAT/BLAST/alignment evidence that would be required. Superfamily-level homology records and annotations cited are not in this bundle but are accurate for 2.08. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Complete and bundle-supported facts: three families, superfamily 51735, lineage, homology scopes, annotations, PF02254. Interprets shared superfamily as positive probable-common-ancestry assertion with family-level divergence; denies shared substrate, catalytic step, cofactor detail, or channel-regulatory role; flags background function statements as unverified; rejects template interchangeability and analogy/convergence claims; lists what evidence would settle open questions. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correctly places both domains in family k.40.1.1 (SUNID 100905) with accurate lineage and SUNIDs, and gives a reasonable designed-protein caveat against natural ancestry. However it never retrieved or mentions the family node's 'not a true family' annotation (must_include 2 and 3), instead stating SCOPe makes a positive family-level homology assertion. Decisive annotation ignored, so bio capped at 2; central annotation missing from factual support. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct: 1.69 d1t1ja_ c.137.1.1 in fold c.137 vs d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1 in c.23, shared nothing below class; 2.08 d1t1ja1 c.23.14.2 under c.23.14 with d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1. States deepest shared homology-bearing level is now the superfamily, supporting probable common ancestry only, not family or biochemistry; distinguishes superfamily naming change from membership change and notes family node 110461 reparented. Minor: 'SCOPe 1.69' label. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct artifact lineage, warning, and homology_implied_by_level=false; d1a14h1 H:9-111 b.1.1.1 V-set identified. Recommends filtering tag hits before any family/superfamily/fold inference. The 'Fab NC10 Fv' detail and claim of retrieving chain listings are not in the cited bundle but are accurate and noncentral. Limits stated (sequence not retrieved, no hits checked).

Thorough and well-supported: 1.75 whole-chain f.11.1.1 and 2.08 split to b.179.1.1/f.60.1.1 with boundaries, and an explicit statement that placement establishes neither common ancestry nor independent origin. Correctly handles 3tewA (in bundle) and function. Only 1.75 and 2.08 queried, so the 2.04 first-split release is not identified.

Complete: SIDs, boundaries, SCCS, superfamily members all supported by bundle. Correctly identifies d3jb9a5 as sole new fold d.394, a4 as only family-level link, a1-a3 as superfamily-level links; frames mosaic of reused superfamilies plus novel fold; limits on 'newly observed', function transfer, and lack of independent hits stated. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Complete and precise: shared lineage, lengths 51/373/752, 're' inconsistency on two domains, 'single repeat' comment, and the 4cj9 A:259-292 representative repeat with coordinates applying only to d4cj9a_. Correctly declines to transfer repeat boundaries or function and flags the truncated d4cj9a_ comment. Fully backed by a comprehensive parents/annotations/homology/sequence bundle.

Correct metadata supported by bundle; pins release=2.08, cites 2.08-stable, and says to cite 2.08-2026-08-16 in addition when the dated snapshot is used; correctly says periodic does not replace stable. Omits what a periodic update contains (newly classified PDB entries without rewriting older stable-release domains). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Complete, bundle-supported facts for all 1ez3 chains and 1br0 (fragment comment, 'ms' flag, no warnings), d1dn1b_ automated match with 222-residue domain vs 120/124 fragments, and the shared a.47.2.1 lineage. Correctly reads fragment-based fold calls as partial three-helical evidence and 1dn1 B as the longer-coverage record, with honest limits. Overly cautious in refusing to call 1dn1 B the full domain, and does not make the point that the complete domain resolves the fragment-driven spectrin-like resemblance. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Correctly reads superfamily placement as supporting divergence within c.2.1, refuses to call c.2 vs c.3 convergent from placement, notes undetectable ancient divergence remains consistent, and lists required external evidence; convergence from ligand chemistry and catalytic triads explained. c.2.1 family list, c.3, and d.81 lineages verified. However, counting d.81 (GAPDH C-terminal catalytic domain) as a third NAD(P)-binding fold is imprecise, since that domain is not the cofactor-binding unit, and no genuinely distinct NAD(P)-binding superfamily beyond c.2/c.3 is cited.

Correct 2.04 b.23.2.1, 2.08 b.18.1.36 with d1nqdb2 tag, Cry b.18.1.3 unchanged, shared superfamily remote homology with distinct families, no function transfer. Appropriately cautious about CRYIIIA/Cry3A naming and weak structural evidence.

Complete: family assertion stands and hf does not withdraw it; hf correctly defined and scoped; structural conformity to the exemplar is the disputed element; template/superposition use rejected without structural evidence; ligand and mutant annotations not transferable; keep flagged or stratified, exclude from fold-level splits, split by family to avoid leakage; limits on quantitative similarity stated. Release 2.08, lineage, comments, and homology fields all supported by the bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22. Verified lineage, sunids, boundaries, fr semantics, protein nodes, cr9 comment. Flag framed as completeness caveat not reclassification or negative homology claim. Alignment: report coverage over aligned interval separately from identity, low full-length coverage reflects missing segment. Representative: prefer complete non-fragment member, honestly notes quality not retrieved so no ranking, keep d1o5dt2 flagged for protein-level coverage. Diversity: fragment and non-fragment reported separately. Explicit unsafe-transfer rejections and list of missing evidence. Complete.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Provisional new superfamily in fold; family claim correctly rejected; new fold explicitly requires structural mismatch, 'not merely a lack of ancestry evidence'; explicitly avoids analogy/convergence claim; absence-of-evidence caveat; FATCAT similarity is not homology. Reported release/periodic-update facts have no supporting API response in the bundle.

Verified facts (superfamily 56112 in fold 56111, class d; families 56171, 64411 with 64412 and 103302, 88854; homology_implied_by_level true with no warnings; ATP-grasp/PIPK comment) all match the bundle, and the comment is correctly treated as a curator note rather than a placement. Interprets shared superfamily as a homology-bearing assertion of common ancestry for the catalytic core while noting families differ; labels the shared ATP-dependent phosphotransfer mechanism as background knowledge. Explicitly forbids transferring Ser/Thr/Tyr, lipid, aminoglycoside or choline specificity and regulatory-subunit or activation-loop control. Requires release-matched lineages, sequence alignment of recognition/regulatory residues, substrate-bound structures, kinetics/substrate panels, and regulatory-domain evidence. Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.
